{"claim_id": "c2", "code": "import sys, json, torch
sys.path.insert(0, "/root/cases/case_121")
import kernel

dev="cuda"
M,K,N,gs=7,64,65,16
rng=torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(7)
groups=(K+gs-1)//gs
x=(torch.rand((M,K),generator=rng)-.5).half()
codes=torch.randint(0,16,(((K+7)//8)*8,N),generator=rng,dtype=torch.int64)
qw64=torch.zeros(((K+7)//8,N),dtype=torch.int64)
for i in range(8): qw64|=codes[i::8]<<(4*i)
zc=torch.randint(0,16,(groups,((N+7)//8)*8),generator=rng,dtype=torch.int64)
qz64=torch.zeros((groups,(N+7)//8),dtype=torch.int64)
for i in range(8): qz64|=zc[:,i::8]<<(4*i)
sc=(.002+.029*torch.rand((groups,N),generator=rng)).half()
ids=(torch.arange(K)//gs)[torch.randperm(K,generator=rng)].int()

def trial(qw_np, qz_np, tag):
    qw=qw_np.to(dev); qz=qz_np.to(dev)
    t=(x.to(dev),qw,sc.to(dev),qz,ids.to(dev),gs)
    out=kernel.run(*t); ref=kernel.reference(*t)
    err=(out-ref).abs(); tol=0.01+0.001*ref.abs()
    return {"tag":tag,"n_negative_qw":int((qw<0).sum()),"n_negative_qz":int((qz<0).sum()),
            "max_abs_err":err.max().item(),"n_violations":int((err>tol).sum())}

base_qw=qw64.int(); base_qz=qz64.int()
neg_qw=base_qw.clone(); neg_qw[0,::3]=neg_qw[0,::3]|(1<<31)
neg_qz=base_qz.clone(); neg_qz[:,0]=neg_qz[:,0]|(1<<31)
r=[trial(base_qw,base_qz,"control_no_negative"),
   trial(neg_qw,base_qz,"negative_qweight_only"),
   trial(base_qw,neg_qz,"negative_qzeros_only")]
print(json.dumps({"claim":"c2","M,K,N":[M,K,N],
 "metric":"paired comparison: violations with vs without negative words on identical low nibbles; isolates sign-extension effect from general packing bug",
 "results":r}))
", "expected_signal": "negative-word trials have substantially larger violations than the no-negative control; if control already fails, c2 specifically is only confirmed if negative words add error"}

message.reasoning_content:
All three probes show massive violations across all shapes — including even shape-consistent ones. Wait, even (65,16,65) fails. This suggests the kernel is generally broken, not just at residues. Even case (7,3,1) passed with 0 errors. Interesting: (1,1,1) and (7,3,1) pass (single group, tiny). Everything else fails. Note make_inputs defaults: rows=7, K=64, N=65 — hmm, that would fail too? The c2 case (7,64,65) with defaults-like input showed violations too... wait c2 modified nibbles with bit31, which changes the low 8 nibbles? No — bit31 set makes word negative, used low nibbles unchanged. But violation was 434. Actually c1 case (7,20,65) etc all fail. So even the default make_inputs shape fails. Let me verify make_inputs default passes or fails — that's decisive. Also note the discrepancies could be due to error in my probe vs reference comparison? reference uses the same validate. It's plausible the kernel is genuinely broken broadly (e.g., sorted order handling: order = argsort(g_idx) maps sorted position->original; but the reference decodes in original order; kernel uses order[sorted_k] as original k for both X load and qweight load — consistent). Yet errors everywhere.

Actually, likely cause: repack's decode arithmetic original_k//8, original_k%8 — original_k is int32 from ORDER, fine. Hmm. Whatever the root cause, runtime evidence shows failures. Let me run one quick probe: make_inputs default case, plus negative-word-free case to distinguish c2. Actually c2 needs isolation: a case that only differs by negative words. Since (7,64,65) without negatives... we don't have that data point. c1 cases (all non-negative) fail broadly, so negative words not needed. For c2 specifically I should run a control: same input without bit31 set. If that also fails (it will, presumably, per c1 pattern), then c2's specific cause is confounded — mark c2 inconclusive or reframe.

Plan this turn: finalize t9 (c1 confirmed), finalize t11 (c3 confirmed), and launch a c2 control probe (same input, no negative words) to isolate. Then next turn finalize c2.
